title: 1 · The Study landing
what: Where a member starts: Desk → Courses. The 'Your trail is a chart' block, the eight Method stations, the Foundations row.
judge: Does it make you want to start? Is it obvious what to tap first? Does the trail-as-a-chart idea land, or is it decoration?

title: 2 · A drill question
what: Today's set, 10 questions. Answer three or four so you see different kinds: a chart question, a wording question, a sizing question.
judge: The wording. The chart. The choices. Is this a question you would ask a student, in your words? Too easy, too hard, pointless?

title: 3 · The answer card
what: After Check: Correct/Wrong, ticker and date, the lesson paragraph, the 'Why' fold, 'Review this one'.
judge: Does the card TEACH, or just mark you? Is the lesson in your voice? Right length? Is the chart annotated enough to see the point?

title: 4 · The end card
what: Keep answering to the end of the 10. The end card: score, XP, streak, what to do next.
judge: Does finishing feel like anything? Would you come back tomorrow because of this screen?

title: 5 · The Practise sheet
what: The sheet with three doors: review my misses, refresh a stale skill, keep going on the trail.
judge: Are these the three things a member wants? Names clear? Anything missing (a timed sprint, a chart-only mode, a pick-a-setup mode)?

title: 6 · A station and its units
what: On the landing tap the 'Setup' station, then a unit on its trail. This is the Duolingo-style path: units in a row, levels inside.
judge: Is the path readable? Do you understand where you are and what comes next? Is 'unit' even the right size of thing?

title: 7 · Foundations (empty today)
what: Scroll to the Foundations row: Market basics, Chart reading, Candlesticks... all 'coming soon' except the 600 candle charts behind Candlesticks.
judge: This is the beginner course. What should the FIRST lesson a brand-new member plays look like? Say it in a sentence or two.

title: 8 · Your review screen
what: The admin screen where you grade items one by one (Type / Skill / Lane filters, N for next, approve / needs fix / reject).
judge: Is this how you want to review? Four at a time on the phone was tiring. What would make reviewing fast and even fun?

title: 9 · The whole thing
what: Everything you just saw, as one product.
judge: You said 2 out of 100. Describe the 100: what a member does in their first five minutes, and what they feel when they close it.
